title: Autism Support Worker - Oxford
description:
Autism Support Worker - Oxford

Are you looking for a role where you can make a difference? Are you interested in gaining hands on experience to support your career?

A great opportunity is available for an Autism Support Worker in a lovely school in Oxford. You will be working directly with students who need additional support with managing their workload in class.

The role:
- This a role where no two days are the same and where every day will bring something new. The school requires a positive, enthusiastic and resilient individual to join their team.
- The school support children between the ages of 4 and 16 with a primary need of Autism but the students have other coexisting needs such as speech and language, behavioural and mental health.
- As an Autism Support Worker, you would be directly involved in helping children with their daily tasks and help maintain a positive and engaging learning environment. You will be required to help the class teacher prepare learning materials and lessons for the day and help keep track of children's progress.
- This is a great opportunity for aspiring psychologists, teachers or therapists. Those with an interest in the education sector will also benefit from this valuable experience. Graduates will be considered.

The ideal Autism Support Worker:
- Would have some experience working with SEN children
- Be patient, nurturing and keen to learn
- Have excellent communication skills
- Understand the importance of Safeguarding
- Bring a fun element to the classroom

Key Information:
- Oxford
- ASAP Start / September Start
- Mon - Fri role
- Full time - long term
- £90 - £100 per day
- Autism Support Worker

If you are interested in this role, you can apply directly to this advert.

Autism Support Worker - Oxford - ASAP / September Start - Mental Health Support

Salary will be determined by the successful candidate's qualifications and relevant experience, and will be in accordance with the client's pay policy.

title: Learning Support Assistant
description:
Learning Support Assistant - Key Stage 3-5

Join Swalcliffe Park School's supportive specialist education team helping secondary-age students learn, build independence and access opportunities in school and the community. You'll need experience in education or youth/community work and strong teamwork skills.

If you've also worked in the following roles, we'd also like to hear from you: Teaching Assistant, SEN Teaching Assistant, Classroom Assistant, Learning Mentor, Student Support Officer, Pastoral Support Officer, Pastoral Support Worker, SEN Support Assistant

SALARY: £26,016 to £26,847 per annum Actual (NJC Scp 4-6)

BENEFITS: Generous Holiday (13 weeks' paid holiday to be taken in school holidays), NEST Pension Scheme, Sickness entitlement 2 weeks full pay 2 weeks half pay and free lunchtime meal

LOCATION: Swalcliffe, Nr Banbury, Oxfordshire

JOB TYPE: Full-Time, Term-Time, Permanent

WORKING HOURS: 37.5 Hours per Week, 39 Weeks Term Time

JOB OVERVIEW

Make a meaningful contribution to students' learning, independence and inclusion in a supportive specialist education environment.

Swalcliffe Park School provides specialist residential education and care for around 70-75 secondary aged boys (10-19 yrs) all of whom are on the Autism Spectrum. We offer excellent working conditions in a beautiful environment, including paid school holidays, opportunities for career development and staff training.

Working within a Key Stage team, the Learning Support Assistant helps individuals and groups access classroom, community and off-site learning while contributing to progress, safeguarding and wellbeing.

The Learning Support Assistant works closely with teachers, therapists, senior leaders and residential colleagues, with opportunities to build skills through training and development.

Across school life, the Learning Support Assistant also supports families, reporting, key-working and the smooth running of education provision.

DUTIES

Your duties as the Learning Support Assistant include:
- Student Learning Support: Work effectively with individuals and groups in the classroom, supporting learning, independence and social inclusion
- Homework, Revision and Exams: Support homework, assignments, revision and exam access arrangements
- Observation and Target Setting: Observe behaviour and learning styles to inform targets and student support
- Interventions and Data: Support teacher, therapist and literacy interventions, collect progress data and maintain records on school systems
- Community and Off-Site Access: Support learning in the community and off-site programmes, including driving school transport where required
- Key Worker Support: Act as key worker for nominated students and support communication with families
- Safeguarding and Safety: Follow safeguarding, child protection, health and safety, risk assessment and safe-working procedures
- Multi-Disciplinary Working: Work collaboratively with teachers, therapists, residential colleagues and other professionals
- School Operations: Supervise break and lunchtime, support whole-school events and provide cover for absent colleagues
- Professional Development: Take part in mentoring, appraisal and training, maintaining knowledge relevant to autism support

CANDIDATE REQUIREMENTS

Essential
- GCSE English Language and Mathematics at Grade 4/C or above (or equivalent)
- Experience of working with young people in an educational or youth/community setting
- Strong interpersonal and teamwork skills with a student-centred approach
- Awareness of safeguarding, confidentiality, and professional boundaries
- IT proficiency, including Word, Excel and email
- Full UK driving licence, with eligibility and willingness to drive school vehicles (subject to insurance)

Desirable
- Experience of working with children, young people and/or adults with autism and associated language or communication difficulties
- Experience supporting pupils with Education, Health and Care Plans
- Experience applying safeguarding policies and procedures
- Knowledge of EHC plans, person-centred support, safeguarding, health and safety, data protection, equality and diversity

The school reserves the right to close the advertisement early, should it receive sufficient applications prior to the closing date.

This school is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. The successful candidate will be expected to undertake an enhanced disclosure. We are an equal opportunities employer.

NO AGENCIES PLEASE

APPLY TODAY

By submitting your job application to us you are hereby giving us your express consent to submit your details to our Client for this purpose.

JOB REF: AWDO-P15226

This job is being advertised by AWD online on behalf of Swalcliffe Park School

title: Emotional Support Worker - Kidlington
description:
Emotional Support Worker - Kidlington

Looking for a role where every day truly matters? Join this amazing specialist school in Kidlington, who support primary and secondary aged students with emotional regulation, social, and mental health needs and help them feel safe, understood, and ready to learn.

About Us

This school is a warm, welcoming space designed for young people who may find mainstream education overwhelming. Many of the students experience challenges with emotional regulation, social interaction, and mental health but here, they're met with patience, understanding, and genuine care.

They believe every child deserves to feel heard, valued, and capable of success and that's where you come in.

Your Role

As an Emotional Support Worker, you'll be a trusted adult, a calm presence, and a positive role model. You'll work closely with students who may feel anxious, frustrated, or disconnected, helping them build confidence, manage emotions, and develop meaningful relationships.

What you'll be doing:
- Supporting students 1:1 and in small groups with their emotional and social development
- Helping young people understand and manage their feelings in a safe, supportive way
- Building strong, trusting relationships that help students feel secure
- Supporting students through challenging moments with patience and care
- Encouraging positive behaviour and celebrating small wins every day
- Helping students develop social skills, confidence, and resilience
- Working closely with teachers, families, and therapists to provide joined-up support

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who is:
- Calm, patient, and understanding
- Passionate about supporting children with additional needs
- Able to stay positive and consistent
- Interested in emotional wellbeing, mental health, or education
- Experienced in working with children or young people (this is a bonus, not a must!)

Key Details
- Location: Kidlington
- Pay: £85-£110 per day (depending on experience)
- Start Date: ASAP
- Hours: Full-time, long-term
- Setting: Specialist school (Primary & Secondary) supporting SEMH and complex needs

Why Join Us?

This isn't just a job-it's a chance to change lives (including your own). Whether you're considering a career in education, psychology, or youth work, or simply want to make a difference, this role offers purpose, growth, and real connection.

Every small breakthrough is a big win here.

Ready to make an impact?
Apply now to become an Emotional Support Worker in Maidenhead and be part of something truly meaningful.

Salary will be determined by the successful candidate's qualifications and relevant experience, and will be in accordance with the client's pay policy.
